title: Reconcile delayed rate-limit refunds and annotate Stripe/NetSuite exports
creator: Maya Patel
description: Several customers have received invoices that do not reflect retroactive rate-limit refunds (credits) issued by the rate-limiter service. The root cause appears to be the timing mismatch between when refunds are created, when they are persisted to the usage ledger, and when the nightly Stripe/NetSuite export job snapshots invoice line allocations. This ticket designs and implements a reconciliation path to surface, annotate, and export late credits so invoices and NetSuite exports remain accurate and auditable.
problem_statement: When rate-limiter refunds are issued after the regular billing snapshot window (e.g., refunds for bursts or manual quota overrides), the export pipeline either drops the credit or creates duplicate/incorrect invoice lines in Stripe and duplicate GL lines in NetSuite. This causes customer confusion, revenue accounting drift, and manual finance adjustments.
impact_summary: Affects invoicing accuracy for any customer that triggers rate-limit credits outside the billing window. Finance team has reported a ~0.4% variance on a recent weekly export and two manual adjustment requests from enterprise customers in the last quarter.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a customer with a per-minute rate limit and burst credits enabled.
2) Exhaust the quota and trigger a rate-limit refund via the rate-limiter admin UI or API (simulate a policy rollback) after the billing snapshot for the day has completed.
3) Run billing export pipeline (simulate nightly export) and observe the absence or misattribution of the refund in the generated Stripe invoice lines.
4) Run NetSuite export and reconcile ledger entries: note mismatched GL lines and missing memo about refund origin.
proposed_solution: Add a reconciliation layer that: (a) captures late refund events and writes a canonical refund annotation record to the usage ledger with a unique export_batch_id, (b) modifies the export job to include 'late_event' annotations and to idempotently attach refunds to the original invoice or create a separate credit memo line when appropriate, and (c) implements a backfill job that replays late annotations into prior exports and emits adjustment files for NetSuite. The design emphasizes idempotency, auditability, and minimal disruption to live invoice generation.
technical_design_notes: - Introduce table billing.late_event_annotations(ref_id UUID, event_type TEXT, origin_service TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, created_at TIMESTAMP, export_batch_id TEXT, processed BOOLEAN, stripe_memo TEXT)

- Export job change: during export, join invoices with billing.late_event_annotations where processed = false and created_at <= export_cutoff + 30d (configurable window). Mark processed = true only after successful Stripe/NetSuite export and verification.
- Add idempotency key: 'export_batch_id' + 'annotation_ref_id' to ensure re-runs do not create duplicate credits in Stripe.
- Backfill job: incremental windowed replayer that can run in 'dry-run' mode and produce a net adjustments CSV for finance if manual reconciliation is preferred.

- Add automatic reconcile heuristics: if original invoice still editable (< 30 days) attach credit memo to invoice; otherwise, create a separate credit invoice and reference original invoice id in metadata.
- PR/Schema: SQL migration PR #r/stripe-billing/348; Reconciler service change PR #r/billing-reconciler/512
acceptance_criteria: 1) New late_event_annotations table exists and is populated by a simulated late refund event in staging.
2) Nightly export includes the annotation and either attaches a credit memo to the invoice or creates a separate credit line; Stripe test-mode shows no duplicate credits after repeated exports.
3) NetSuite export files include explicit memo fields for late credits and are accepted by the finance import flow in sandbox without errors.
4) Backfill tooling can be run by finance with a dry-run that produces a reconciliation report tracing original refund events to exported adjustment rows.
5) Monitoring dashboards show processed=false count trending to zero after backfill; any remaining items are surfaced in alerts.
6) Unit/integration tests cover idempotency semantics for export re-runs.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Duplicate credits if export idempotency not perfectly enforced. Mitigation: use strong idempotency keys and test repeated export runs in staging against Stripe sandbox.
Risk: Accounting mismatch for >90-day invoices. Mitigation: restrict automatic attachment to invoices <30 days and route older events to finance for manual adjustments; document policy.
Risk: Backfill volume causing heavy DB load. Mitigation: windowed replay with rate-limits, resume tokens, and offline CSV generation option.
Risk: NetSuite format mismatch. Mitigation: include NetSuite sandbox import in acceptance tests and add a flag to produce finance-ready spreadsheets instead of automatic push.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge schema migration and reconciler changes behind feature flag 'late_credit_export_v1'.
2) Deploy to staging; run synthetic scenario tests and finance sandbox imports.
3) Enable feature flag for a single low-risk customer cohort for 7 days; monitor invoices and exports.
4) Run backfill on historical window (configurable 30/60/90 days) in dry-run and review with finance.
5) Gradually enable globally and remove feature flag after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
monitoring_queries: - SQL: SELECT count(*) FROM billing.late_event_annotations WHERE processed = false;
- SQL: SELECT export_batch_id, COUNT(*) FROM billing.late_event_annotations WHERE processed = true GROUP BY export_batch_id;
manual_run_instructions: 1) To simulate late refund: POST /admin/rate-limiter/refund {customer_id, amount_cents, reason}.
2) Verify: SELECT * FROM billing.late_event_annotations WHERE origin_service='rate-limiter' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;
4) If Stripe failures: inspect /tmp/stripe_export_test.log and use idempotency key from logs to dedupe manually via Stripe UI.
